title: Microbial allies: Enhancing plant defense via phenylpropanoid pathway and lignification
content: Plants encounter a diverse range of microorganisms, including both pathogens and beneficial microbes. While pathogens trigger plant defense responses, beneficial microbes, such as certain rhizobacteria, can induce systemic resistance, priming the plant immune system to combat future threats. Similar to pathogen-induced resistance, induced systemic resistance involves a complex interplay of metabolic pathways, hormonal signaling, and immune components, characterized by the accumulation of reactive oxygen species, activation of defense-related genes, and production of pathogenesis-related proteins (Pieterse et al. 2014; De Kesel et al. 2021).
